items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new heuristic is hard to follow and barely commented: `if sep and scheme and scheme[0].isalpha() and all(c.isalnum() or c in '+-.' for c in scheme):` followed by nested `'.' not in scheme or rest.startswith('/')`. The original explanatory comment about the netloc/path swap was removed.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Hand-rolled string parsing replaces the existing `parse_url` helper. The diff also changes unrelated code: `get_auth_from_url` now calls prepend, and `sessions.py` changes `if username and password` to `if username`. The project context says a one-line auth re-join was enough.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Fragile scheme-detection heuristics stand in for a real parser. f-strings (`f'{new_scheme}://{url}'`) break Python 2.7, which requests 2.27 still supported. Some edge cases, such as `localhost:8080`, are now misclassified as having a scheme.

items.name: prepend_scheme_if_needed public behaviour unchanged otherwise
items.name_zh: prepend_scheme_if_needed 其他公开行为不变
items.evidence: No-auth behaviour changed. Under the new heuristic, `'localhost:8080'` (alnum scheme, no dot, rest has no '/') is returned unchanged instead of `http://localhost:8080`. The function was rewritten from scratch rather than just re-joining parse_url's `auth` onto netloc.
